definition: Restrictions on how many requests or how much data a user or application can send to a system within a given time period.
details: Rate limiting is used by AI API providers to manage infrastructure load, ensure fair access across customers, and mitigate abuse such as automated scraping or denial-of-service attempts.

explainer.lead: Rate limiting restricts how many requests or how much data a user or application can send to a system in a given time period. It matters because it keeps infrastructure load manageable and access fair.

tiers.eli5: It is like a turnstile that only lets a certain number of people through each minute so the line stays orderly.
tiers.practitioner: AI API providers use rate limiting to manage load, ensure fair access across customers, and mitigate abuse such as automated scraping or denial-of-service attempts; a pitfall is setting limits without handling throttled clients gracefully.
tiers.paperLevel: Restrictions on how many requests or how much data a user or application can send to a system within a given time period; used by AI API providers for load management, fair access, and abuse mitigation.

explainer.example: An API provider returns errors to a client that exceeds its per-minute request allowance.
